questions.question: On the Oxford/MRC scale a muscle that can move the part through full range actively but only with gravity eliminated is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 2: full range gravity-eliminated. Grade 3: full range against gravity. Grade 1: palpable contraction only. Grade 0: no contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A muscle that completes the full available range against gravity but cannot tolerate any added resistance is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 (Fair) = full range against gravity without resistance. Grade 4 tolerates moderate resistance, grade 5 maximal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient shows a visible or palpable contraction of a muscle but no joint movement. The grade is:
questions.explanation: A flicker of contraction without movement is grade 1 (Trace).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a ‘break test’ of manual muscle testing, the therapist:

options.A: Asks the patient to push as hard as possible against a fixed hand
options.B: Passively moves the joint to find end range
options.C: Allows the patient to move through full range against gravity only
options.D: Applies resistance gradually until the patient can no longer hold the position

questions.explanation: The break test (Daniels) applies resistance until the muscle ‘breaks’; the make test uses an isometric contraction against a fixed resistance without breaking the hold.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which factor would NOT normally invalidate a manual muscle test?

options.B: Poor patient understanding of the command
options.C: Testing in the standard position with proper stabilisation

questions.explanation: Pain, substitution and misunderstanding reduce reliability; correct positioning and stabilisation increase it.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the standard manual muscle test for the gluteus medius the patient lies:

options.A: Supine with the hip flexed to 90°
options.C: On the side with the test leg uppermost, abducting in slight extension and lateral rotation neutral
options.D: Prone with the knee flexed to 90°

questions.explanation: Side-lying with the hip slightly extended and neutral rotation to avoid substitution by TFL (flexion/medial rotation) and the hip flexors.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Weakness of serratus anterior is best demonstrated by:

options.A: Winging of the scapula when the arm is pushed forward against resistance
options.B: Inability to abduct the arm past 90° only
options.C: Loss of sensation in the deltoid area

questions.explanation: Long thoracic nerve palsy causes medial border winging on forward pushing or wall push-up.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The standard position to test grade 3 knee extension (quadriceps) is:

options.A: Sitting with the knee over the edge of the plinth, extending the knee against gravity

questions.explanation: Sitting (thigh supported) lets the patient extend the knee against gravity; resistance is given at the distal leg for grade 4–5.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which muscle acts as the prime mover in the initial 0–15° of shoulder abduction?
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus initiates abduction (0–15°), the middle deltoid is the main abductor from 15–90°, then trapezius and serratus anterior rotate the scapula for elevation above 90°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Testing the medial hamstrings in prone requires the hip to be:

options.A: Laterally rotated with the knee extended
options.B: Slightly medially rotated with the knee flexed, resistance on the distal leg

questions.explanation: Medial rotation of the hip with knee flexion isolates semitendinosus and semimembranosus; lateral rotation emphasises biceps femoris.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the neutral zero method of recording joint range, the anatomical position is taken as:

options.A: 0° for all joints (except forearm in mid-rotation)

questions.explanation: The neutral zero method (Cave and Roberts) records all motion from the anatomical position, so normal extension of the elbow is 0° and flexion 135–150°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A knee extends actively 5° beyond neutral and flexes to 60°. The correct recording is:
questions.explanation: Hyperextension is recorded first (5), then 0, then flexion (60). Total range = 65°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A knee moves from 15° of flexion (cannot extend further) to 90° of flexion. The total available range of motion is:
questions.explanation: Total arc = end − start = 90 − 15 = 75°. It would be recorded as 15–90° (extension lag/flexion contracture of 15°).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: For measuring elbow flexion with a universal goniometer, the axis is placed over the:
questions.explanation: Fixed arm along the humerus toward the acromion, moving arm along the radius toward the radial styloid, axis at the lateral epicondyle.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal active range of shoulder flexion (AAOS) is approximately:
questions.explanation: AAOS norms: shoulder flexion 0–180°, abduction 0–180°, extension 0–60°, medial rotation 0–70°, lateral rotation 0–90°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal range of hip flexion (knee flexed) is approximately:
questions.explanation: AAOS: hip flexion 0–120°, extension 0–30°, abduction 0–45°, adduction 0–30°, medial/lateral rotation 0–45°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal range of ankle dorsiflexion is about:
questions.explanation: AAOS: ankle dorsiflexion 0–20°, plantar flexion 0–50°, inversion 0–35°, eversion 0–15°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To improve the reliability of goniometric measurement between sessions you should:

options.A: Use the same patient position, landmarks, instrument and preferably the same tester
options.B: Change landmarks each time to avoid bias

questions.explanation: Standardising technique reduces error; intratester reliability is better than inter-tester.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal end-feel at the end of elbow flexion with bulky biceps (soft tissue approximation) is:
questions.explanation: Soft end-feel = approximation of soft tissue (knee/elbow flexion). Hard = bone on bone (elbow extension); firm = capsule/ligament stretch (shoulder lateral rotation).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A hard (bone-to-bone) end-feel is normal at the end of:
questions.explanation: Olecranon contacting the olecranon fossa produces a hard end-feel at full elbow extension.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An empty end-feel is typically caused by:

options.D: Severe pain preventing the end of range from being reached (e.g. acute bursitis or tumour)

questions.explanation: In an empty end-feel the patient stops the examiner because of pain before any structure resistance is felt; it is a red flag for serious pathology.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A firm, leathery end-feel before the normal end of range suggests:
questions.explanation: Firm end-feel = capsular/ligamentous resistance; early muscle spasm gives a ‘springy’ stop; a loose body gives a springy block.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the knee joint is:
questions.explanation: Cyriax: knee = flexion > extension (e.g. 'gross loss of flexion, slight loss of extension'). Hip = flexion, abduction, medial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the hip joint is:

options.A: Limitation of flexion, abduction and medial rotation
options.D: Limitation of extension and adduction only

questions.explanation: Hip capsular pattern: flexion, abduction and medial rotation are the most restricted; seen in osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Resisted isometric movement that is strong and painful suggests a lesion of:
questions.explanation: Cyriax: pain on resisted testing with full passive range indicates a contractile lesion; painful passive and active movement (non-contractile) suggests an inert structure.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The close-packed position of the knee joint is:
questions.explanation: Close-packed (maximum congruency and ligament tension): knee full extension; hip extension with medial rotation; elbow extension; shoulder abduction with lateral rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The resting (loose-packed) position of the glenohumeral joint is:

options.A: 55° abduction, 30° horizontal adduction, slight lateral rotation

questions.explanation: Loose-packed positions are used for mobilisation; shoulder ~55° abduction and 30° horizontal adduction.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In Maitland's mobilisation scale, Grade IV movement is:

options.A: A small-amplitude movement at the beginning of the range
options.B: A large-amplitude movement within the range
options.D: A small-amplitude oscillation at the end of the available range

questions.explanation: Grades I–II: smaller/larger amplitude in the first half of range (pain relief). Grades III–IV: into resistance, large (III) or small (IV) amplitude to stretch. Grade V: manipulation (thrust).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: For a very painful, irritable joint, the most appropriate Maitland mobilisation is:

options.A: Grade IV at the end of range
options.C: Grade I–II oscillations, within the pain-free range

questions.explanation: Gentle low-grade oscillations stimulate mechanoreceptors and inhibit pain (gate control) without provoking the irritable tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A Grade V Maitland movement is:

options.B: A passive stretch within pain-free range
options.C: A small-amplitude, high-velocity thrust at the end of range

questions.explanation: Manipulation: small-amplitude, high-speed thrust beyond the elastic barrier, often with an audible cavitation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the Kaltenborn system, Grade II traction/glide is applied to:

options.B: Take up the slack in the tissues

questions.explanation: Grade I: loosening (unload). Grade II: take up slack. Grade III: stretch tissue around the joint.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When a concave joint surface moves on a fixed convex surface, the glide occurs:

options.D: In the same direction as the bone movement

questions.explanation: Concave on convex: glide in the SAME direction as the bone moves. Convex on concave: glide in the OPPOSITE direction.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To increase knee flexion by joint mobilisation, the tibia (concave) should be glided:
questions.explanation: The tibial plateau is concave, so it glides in the same direction as the shaft moves in flexion (posterior). The patella is also glided inferiorly for flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which patellar glide is needed to improve knee FLEXION?
questions.explanation: As the knee flexes the patella slides distally; a restricted inferior glide limits flexion, whereas a restricted superior glide limits extension.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An absolute contraindication to spinal manipulation is:

options.A: Mechanical low back pain without red flags
options.C: Cauda equina syndrome or spinal cord compression

questions.explanation: Red flags such as cauda equina syndrome, fracture, infection, malignancy and vertebrobasilar insufficiency contraindicate thrust techniques.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Before cervical manipulation, which test screens for vertebrobasilar insufficiency?
questions.explanation: Sustained extension/rotation tests look for dizziness, nystagmus, diplopia, drop attacks (the 5 Ds and 3 Ns).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Muscle energy technique (MET) uses:

options.A: The patient's own isometric contraction against a counterforce, followed by relaxation and stretch

questions.explanation: MET (Mitchell): patient contracts a muscle isometrically against a controlled counterforce (post-isometric relaxation), then the therapist takes up the new barrier.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Thomas test is used to assess:
questions.explanation: Patient supine, one hip fully flexed to flatten the lumbar spine; the opposite thigh lifting off the couch indicates a hip flexion contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Ober's test is performed to identify tightness of the:

options.B: Iliotibial band and tensor fasciae latae

questions.explanation: Side-lying; hip abducted and extended then lowered; failure of the thigh to drop below horizontal indicates ITB/TFL tightness.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive straight leg raise (Lasegue) test for lumbar disc prolapse reproduces:

options.B: Pain at 90° only in the hamstrings
options.C: Radicular leg pain between about 30° and 70° of hip flexion

questions.explanation: Neural tension on the sciatic nerve roots L5/S1 typically produces leg pain before 70°; hamstring tightness gives pain at the posterior thigh only.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The slump test is primarily a test of:

options.D: Neural tension in the spinal cord, nerve roots and sciatic nerve

questions.explanation: The patient sits slumped, flexes the neck, extends the knee and dorsiflexes the ankle; reproduction of symptoms that ease with neck extension suggests adverse neural tension.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Phalen's test (wrist flexion held for 60 seconds) is positive in:
questions.explanation: Sustained wrist flexion compresses the median nerve, producing paraesthesia in its distribution in carpal tunnel syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Tinel's sign is elicited by:

options.C: Percussing over a nerve to produce tingling in its distribution

questions.explanation: A positive Tinel's (distal tingling on percussion) marks a regenerating nerve front or a compressed nerve (e.g. carpal tunnel).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Finkelstein's test is used to diagnose:
questions.explanation: The thumb is flexed into the palm and the wrist passively deviated ulnarward; pain over the first dorsal compartment is positive.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pain over the lateral epicondyle on resisted wrist extension with the elbow extended and forearm pronated (Cozen's test) indicates:
questions.explanation: Cozen's and Mill's tests stress the common extensor origin (ECRB) to reproduce lateral elbow pain.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow) is aggravated by:

options.D: Resisted wrist flexion and forearm pronation

questions.explanation: The common flexor/pronator origin is overloaded; resisted wrist flexion reproduces the pain.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The drop arm test assesses integrity of the:
questions.explanation: The patient cannot slowly lower an abducted arm from 90° in a full-thickness rotator cuff tear.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Neer and Hawkins–Kennedy tests are used to detect:
questions.explanation: Passive forced flexion (Neer) or flexion with medial rotation at 90° (Hawkins) squeezes the supraspinatus against the coracoacromial arch.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Adson's test is positive when:

options.A: The radial pulse diminishes with the neck extended and rotated toward the tested side with deep inspiration (thoracic outlet syndrome)
options.D: The hand tingles on percussion of the median nerve

questions.explanation: Adson's test checks for scalene compression of the subclavian artery; roos and Wright tests are also used.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The anterior drawer test of the knee primarily assesses:
questions.explanation: With the knee at 90° flexion, anterior translation of the tibia on the femur >6–8 mm beyond the other side indicates ACL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A valgus stress applied to the knee at 30° of flexion tests the:
questions.explanation: Valgus stress opens the medial side; varus stress tests the lateral collateral ligament.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The patellar apprehension test is positive in:
questions.explanation: The examiner pushes the patella laterally with the knee slightly flexed; apprehension and quadriceps contraction suggest recurrent lateral subluxation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Homans' sign (calf pain on passive dorsiflexion) is used to detect:
questions.explanation: Homans' sign has low specificity; DVT should be confirmed by Doppler or D-dimer. Never massage a leg with suspected DVT.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Trendelenburg test is positive when:

options.B: The pelvis drops on the unsupported side while standing on one leg
options.C: The pelvis rises on the unsupported side

questions.explanation: Weak hip abductors on the stance side let the pelvis drop on the opposite side.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The FABER (Patrick's) test assesses the:
questions.explanation: Flexion, abduction and external rotation of the hip stress the hip and SI joint; groin pain indicates hip pathology, posterior pain the SI joint.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Spurling's test (neck extension, side-flexion with axial compression) is used to detect:
questions.explanation: Reduction of the intervertebral foramen reproduces arm pain in nerve root compression.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Froment's sign is a test for:
questions.explanation: When gripping a sheet of paper between thumb and index finger, the thumb IP joint flexes (FPL, median nerve) to compensate for a paralysed adductor pollicis.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The anterior drawer test of the ankle stresses the:
questions.explanation: Anterior translation of the talus from the mortise indicates ATFL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The ankle jerk is mainly mediated by which spinal segment?
questions.explanation: Knee jerk L3–L4; ankle jerk S1; biceps jerk C5–C6; triceps C7; supinator C5–C6.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The myotome tested by resisted ankle dorsiflexion is:
questions.explanation: Myotomes: L2 hip flexion, L3 knee extension, L4 ankle dorsiflexion, L5 great toe extension, S1 plantar flexion/eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The dermatome that covers the thumb is:
questions.explanation: C6 thumb, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger. T4 nipple, T10 umbilicus.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which finding would NOT be expected with a C6 root lesion?

options.A: Paraesthesia of the middle and ring fingers
options.B: Sensory loss over the thumb and lateral forearm
options.D: Weakness of biceps and wrist extensors

questions.explanation: C6 root: thumb/index sensory loss, biceps and wrist extension weakness; the middle finger is C7 and ring/little C8.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive Babinski sign (extensor plantar response) in an adult indicates:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexion of the great toe with fanning of the other toes after stroking the lateral sole signifies pyramidal tract disease (normal in infants under about 1 year).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Sustained ankle clonus is a feature of:

options.A: Upper motor neurone lesion with spasticity

questions.explanation: Rapid dorsiflexion elicits rhythmic contractions of the calf in UMN lesions due to increased stretch reflex excitability.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive Romberg test (swaying or falling with the eyes closed) indicates loss of:
questions.explanation: Standing with feet together and eyes closed removes visual compensation; sway indicates a sensory ataxia.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia and past-pointing are signs of:
questions.explanation: Cerebellar dysfunction produces ipsilateral incoordination; Parkinson's gives resting tremor with rigidity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Modified Ashworth Scale is used to grade:
questions.explanation: Graded 0–4 (with 1+): resistance to passive movement. It does not measure strength.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The minimum and maximum scores on the Glasgow Coma Scale are:
questions.explanation: GCS = eye (1–4) + verbal (1–5) + motor (1–6) = 3–15; ≤8 is severe brain injury.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Proprioception and vibration sense are carried in the:
questions.explanation: Dorsal columns: fine touch, vibration, proprioception (ipsilateral until the medulla). Spinothalamic: pain and temperature (contralateral).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a lateral view of normal standing posture the plumb line passes through the:

options.A: Lobe of the ear, acromion, greater trochanter and just anterior to the lateral malleolus

questions.explanation: Kendall's ideal alignment passes just in front of the lateral malleolus, slightly posterior to the patella centre, through the greater trochanter and acromion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A ‘lurching’ gait with the trunk leaning over the affected side during stance suggests:

options.C: Weakness of the hip abductors (gluteus medius gait)

questions.explanation: Trunk shifting over the stance hip reduces the abductor lever; unilateral weakness gives a compensated Trendelenburg gait.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A steppage (high-stepping) gait is seen in:
questions.explanation: Foot drop needs excessive hip and knee flexion to clear the toes; seen in common peroneal palsy, L4–L5 radiculopathy.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a normal walking cycle the stance phase occupies about:
questions.explanation: Stance ≈60% (with double support ≈20%) and swing ≈40%. Running has no double support.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: True leg length is measured from the:

options.B: Anterior superior iliac spine to the medial malleolus
options.C: Greater trochanter to the lateral malleolus

questions.explanation: True length: ASIS to medial malleolus; apparent length: umbilicus (or xiphisternum) to the medial malleolus.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Apparent shortening of the leg with normal true leg length is typically due to:

options.D: Pelvic obliquity (e.g. adduction contracture of the hip)

questions.explanation: True length equal but apparent length reduced implies pelvic tilt or fixed adduction deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To monitor muscle bulk of the thigh over time, girth measurements should be taken:

options.A: At the widest point each time, without landmarks
options.C: Using a flexible ruler held loosely
options.D: At a fixed distance above a bony landmark such as the upper pole of the patella

questions.explanation: Standardising the point (e.g. 10 cm above the patella) allows valid comparison.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A flat back deformity with a decreased lumbar lordosis is commonly associated with:

options.A: Tight hamstrings and posterior pelvic tilt
options.C: Tight hip flexors and anterior pelvic tilt
options.D: Weak abdominals and an exaggerated lordosis

questions.explanation: Tight hamstrings pull the pelvis into posterior tilt, flattening the lumbar curve; hip flexor tightness causes anterior tilt and hyperlordosis.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine is commonly associated with:

options.B: Tight hip flexors and erector spinae with weak abdominals and gluteals

questions.explanation: Lower crossed syndrome (Janda): anterior pelvic tilt from tight hip flexors/lumbar extensors and weak abdominals/gluteals.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A normal resting adult respiratory rate is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal adult resting HR 60–100 bpm, RR 12–20/min, BP <120/80 mmHg, SpO₂ 95–100%.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which pulse is commonly palpated at the wrist on the radial side?
questions.explanation: Radial pulse at the wrist; brachial in the antecubital fossa; carotid in the neck; femoral in the groin; popliteal behind the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Using a cuff that is too narrow when measuring blood pressure will give:
questions.explanation: A narrow cuff requires more pressure to occlude the artery; the cuff bladder width should be about 40% of arm circumference.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
